$meta.purpose: Manufacturer-recommended installation tools for residential solar ELECTRICAL work (microinverter trunk cable, conduit, wiring, interconnection). Drives the 'Suggested Tools' section of the job BOM.
primarySources: Enphase IQ8 Series Microinverter Installation and Operation Manual (enphase.com/download/iq8-series-microinverter-installation-and-operation-manual)
Enphase Q Field Wireable Connector Quick Install Guide (support.enphase.com/s/article/Enphase-Q-Field-Wireable-Connector-Quick-Install-Guide)
Enphase IQ Combiner 4/4C Quick Install Guide (enphase.com/sites/default/files/2021-10/IQ-Combiner-4-4C-QIG-EN-US-Rev03-10-23-2021_0.pdf)
NEC 110.14(D) / NEMA 'Using Torque Tools for Terminating Building Wire' (nema.org technical document library)
NFPA 70E standard electrician practice (PPE for energized/line-side work)

enphase.use: Release locking AC connectors on IQ/Q Cable drops, remove Q-SEAL sealing caps, and disconnect MC4/Amphenol H4 DC connectors and AC module mounts without damaging the connector
enphase.why: Enphase manual states a disconnect tool MUST be used to remove a sealing cap or AC connector; listed in the IQ8 manual's required-accessories list. Sold as a 10-pack; roughly one per crew member
enphase.source: Enphase IQ8 Series Installation and Operation Manual; enphase.com store 'Q Cable Disconnect Tool'

enphase.use: Microinverter mounting hardware and enclosure terminations
enphase.source: Enphase IQ8 Series Installation and Operation Manual, 'Required tools' (screwdrivers, wire cutters, voltmeter, torque wrench, sockets, wrenches)

enphase.tool: Torque wrench + sockets/wrenches for racking hardware
enphase.use: Torque microinverter mounting bolts to racking manufacturer spec
enphase.source: Enphase IQ8 Series Installation and Operation Manual, 'Required tools'

enphase.use: Cut IQ Cable between drops; trim tie wraps
enphase.source: Enphase IQ8 Series Installation and Operation Manual, 'Required tools'

enphase.use: Verify AC branch voltage and absence of voltage before touching terminations; required by the Enphase manual
enphase.source: Enphase IQ8 Series Installation and Operation Manual, 'Required tools'

enphase.tool: Open-end/adjustable wrench for field-wireable connector gland nuts
enphase.use: Tighten Q-CONN-10M/10F field-wireable connector gland nut to 7 N·m (single-phase Q connectors) — do not over-tighten; three-phase QD connectors: cable gland 4.5 N·m, contact-carrier screws 1 N·m
enphase.why: Under-torqued glands lose the connector's ingress-protection rating; over-torque cracks the gland
enphase.source: Enphase Q Field Wireable Connector Quick Install Guide; Enphase three-phase QD field-wireable QIG

enphase.tool: Torque screwdriver (in-lb range) for IQ Combiner terminations
enphase.use: IQ Combiner 4 DG breaker terminals: 20 lb-in (2.2 N·m) for 14-10 AWG, 25 lb-in (2.8 N·m) for 8 AWG; consumption-metering CT terminals ~5 lb-in
enphase.why: Combiner QIG lists screwdriver, pliers, and torque wrench as required tools and tabulates torque per wire gauge
enphase.source: Enphase IQ Combiner 4/4C Quick Install Guide

enphase.tool: IQ Cable accessories on hand (not tools, but required consumables)
enphase.use: Q-SEAL-10 sealing caps for every unused cable drop, Q-TERM-10 terminators (2 per branch typical), Q-CLIP-100 cable clips or UV-rated tie wraps for cable management, Q-CONN-10M/10F field-wireable connectors
enphase.source: Enphase IQ8 Series Installation and Operation Manual, required accessories list

enphase.tool: Connector seating check (click test + tug test)
enphase.use: Push module DC leads and IQ Cable AC connectors together until they audibly click, then pull-test; visually confirm no gap at the connector collar
enphase.why: Partially seated PV connectors are a leading cause of arc faults; Enphase connectors are designed to latch audibly
enphase.source: Enphase IQ8 quick install guide practice; standard installer practice

wireManagement.use: Dispense THHN from 500 ft spools when pulling homerun conductors; holds L1/L2/N/EGC colors simultaneously so a 3-4 conductor pull pays out evenly
wireManagement.why: THHN for #10 and #8 AWG is standardly sold on 500 ft spools (also 1000/2500 ft); a caddy prevents spool tangling and insulation scuffing during pulls
wireManagement.source: Standard trade practice; 500 ft spool size verified at Southwire SIMpull / wireandcableyourway.com listings for #10 and #8 THHN

wireManagement.use: Pull THHN through EMT/PVC conduit runs from roof junction box to combiner/POI; fiberglass preferred near energized equipment
Reduce friction on longer conduit pulls or pulls with multiple bends (fill approaching 40%)
Attach conductor bundle to fish tape for multi-conductor pulls without stressing insulation

wireManagement.tool: UV-rated cable ties and/or Q-CLIP-100 clips
wireManagement.use: Secure IQ Cable to racking rails; keep cable off the roof surface and within bend radius
wireManagement.source: Enphase IQ8 Series Installation and Operation Manual (tie wraps or IQ Cable Clips listed as required)

conduit.use: Bend offsets, kicks, and 90s for the AC homerun raceway; 3/4" EMT is the typical residential solar AC run, 1" for larger backfeed or multi-circuit runs (separate bender head per trade size)
Ream every field-cut EMT end before assembly so burrs cannot skin conductor insulation
conduit.why: NEC 358.28(A) requires cut ends be reamed; nicked THHN in a hot rooftop raceway is a ground-fault seed

conduit.tool: Hacksaw (fine-tooth blade) or portable band saw
conduit.use: Cut EMT to length; band saw gives squarer, faster cuts on repetitive work but a hacksaw is sufficient for residential jobs
Level/plumb conduit runs and equipment enclosures; magnetic face sits on EMT while strapping

conduit.tool: Nut drivers / socket set for conduit straps and strut hardware
conduit.use: Set-screw EMT fittings, one-hole/two-hole straps (strap within 3 ft of every box and every 10 ft per NEC 358.30), strut clamps at service equipment

conduit.tool: Strut/channel accessories: strut cutter or portaband + strut nuts
conduit.use: Mount combiner/disconnect on strut where wall surface is uneven; cut strut cleanly and deburr

conduit.tool: Drill/driver with masonry and wood bits, hole saws
conduit.use: Penetrations for LB fittings, mounting enclosures, attaching straps to stucco/wood

termination.tool: Calibrated torque screwdriver (in-lb) + small torque wrench (ft-lb)
termination.use: Every lug, breaker, and terminal termination: breakers, combiner lugs, disconnect lugs, meter-socket line/load lugs (only where permitted to work), neutral/ground bars
termination.why: NEC 110.14(D) REQUIRES terminations be tightened to the manufacturer's marked torque using a calibrated torque tool or other approved means (2020 NEC allows shear/breakaway indicators). Inspectors increasingly ask to see the torque tool and its calibration certificate
termination.source: NEC 110.14(D); NEMA 'Using Torque Tools for Terminating Building Wire'; IAEI/EC&M code commentary

termination.use: Strip THHN homerun conductors (#10/#8 typical) and equipment whips to the strip length marked on the terminal or connector

termination.tool: Crimper for compression lugs/ferrules (with correct dies)
termination.use: Compression ring terminals or lugs where equipment requires crimped terminations; use the lug manufacturer's listed die and crimp cycle
termination.why: Listed lug + matched die is required for the termination to remain within its listing
termination.source: Standard electrician practice; UL 486A-486B listing requirements

termination.tool: 1000 V insulated hand tools (screwdrivers, pliers, cutters)
termination.use: All work in or near equipment that may be energized — panelboards, meter sockets, supply-side taps

termination.tool: Digital multimeter (CAT III/IV rated) + clamp meter
termination.use: Absence-of-voltage verification before touching terminations; measure per-branch AC current at commissioning to confirm production
termination.source: Enphase IQ8 manual (voltmeter in required tools); NFPA 70E verification practice

termination.use: Optional on Enphase AC-microinverter systems (no long HVDC strings), but useful to prove homerun conductor insulation after pull and required by some AHJs/commissioning checklists; NEVER megger through connected microinverters or the gateway — disconnect electronics first
termination.source: Standard commissioning practice; not listed in the Enphase IQ8 required-tools list

termination.use: Stripe each torqued termination after tightening as visible evidence for the inspector and for QA re-checks
termination.source: Standard trade practice supporting NEC 110.14(D) documentation

termination.use: Apply NEC 690/705 labels (rapid shutdown, backfeed, disconnect directory) at final; UV-rated labels

supplySide.tool: Class 0 rubber insulating gloves (1000 V) with leather protectors
supplySide.use: Any work on or near energized service conductors — supply-side (line-side) connections, meter-socket work where the utility has not dropped service
supplySide.why: Service conductors upstream of the main breaker have no overcurrent protection; NFPA 70E requires shock PPE for energized work. Gloves must be within their 6-month electrical retest date
supplySide.source: NFPA 70E Table 130.7; standard utility/solar interconnection practice

supplySide.tool: Arc-rated face shield + balaclava (or arc-flash suit per incident-energy analysis)
supplySide.use: Energized supply-side terminations and meter pulls; residential services are commonly PPE Category 1-2 but verify per NFPA 70E tables or an incident-energy study

supplySide.tool: 1000 V insulated tool set (dedicated for energized work)
supplySide.use: Supply-side tap connections (e.g., insulation-piercing connectors, Polaris-style taps) and panel work; insulated tools are mandatory when de-energizing is infeasible

supplySide.tool: Voltage tester with proving unit (live-dead-live method)
supplySide.use: Verify absence of voltage on the load side before work; prove the tester before and after
Cover exposed energized parts adjacent to the work area during supply-side connections

commissioning.tool: Smartphone/tablet with Enphase Installer App (Enphase Installer Portal account)
commissioning.use: Scan microinverter serials (per-module map), provision the IQ Gateway/Envoy, set grid profile, verify per-device production and connectivity
commissioning.why: Enphase commissioning is app-driven; the array map ties each micro's serial to its roof position
commissioning.source: Enphase IQ Gateway/Envoy commissioning documentation; Enphase Installer App

commissioning.tool: Wi-Fi/Ethernet/cellular connectivity for the IQ Gateway
commissioning.use: Gateway needs internet (customer Wi-Fi, Ethernet, or Mobile Connect cellular kit) to report to Enphase App/Enlighten; verify signal at the combiner location during commissioning
Confirm per-branch AC amperage roughly matches expected output at current irradiance; sanity-check CT orientation for consumption metering

OPTIONAL for residential Enphase jobs — per-panel monitoring already reveals underperformers; an irradiance meter only matters for formal capacity-test commissioning (more common on commercial/PPA jobs)
commissioning.source: Standard commissioning practice; not an Enphase requirement

commissioning.use: Verify every marked termination still shows an unbroken torque stripe before inspection
Photograph torque marks, label placement, connector seating, and open equipment before covers go on — many AHJs and financiers require photo documentation

caveats: Torque values cited (Q field-wireable gland 7 N.m single-phase, QD gland 4.5 N.m / carrier screws 1 N.m three-phase; IQ Combiner 4 DG breaker 20 lb-in for 14-10 AWG, 25 lb-in for 8 AWG, CT terminals ~5 lb-in) come from Enphase quick-install guides found via web search on 2026-07-11 — FIELD-VERIFY against the exact revision of the manual shipped with the hardware before printing on customer-facing documents.

Q-DISC-10 SKU verified against Enphase store and multiple distributors; other Enphase accessory SKUs (Q-SEAL-10, Q-TERM-10, Q-CLIP-100, Q-CONN-10M/10F) are from the IQ8 manual accessory list — newer IQ8 'commercial'/QD product lines use different (QD-prefixed) part numbers, so match the SKU family to the microinverter generation on the BOM.

NEC 110.14(D): 2017 NEC required a 'calibrated torque tool'; 2020+ NEC says 'an approved means' (torque tool, or shear/breakaway indicator hardware). Which edition applies depends on the AHJ's adopted code cycle.

PPE category for supply-side work is site-specific: NFPA 70E table method or incident-energy analysis governs. Class 0 gloves (1000 V) are the common residential floor, but do not print PPE guidance as sufficient without a qualified-person determination.

Insulation-resistance (megger) testing is NOT in the Enphase required-tools list; if performed, all microinverters, the gateway, and any surge devices must be disconnected first or they can be damaged.
Irradiance meter marked optional — no manufacturer requirement found for residential Enphase commissioning.
EMT bender trade sizes listed (1/2", 3/4", 1") reflect typical residential solar AC runs; actual size comes from the project's conduit fill/conductor schedule, not this list.
No pricing included intentionally — tool pricing varies too much by brand/vendor to hard-code.
This file is suggestion-level content for a BOM 'Suggested Tools' section, not an exhaustive safety program; it does not replace NFPA 70E training, manufacturer manuals, or AHJ requirements.
